# prism-source Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Source: Decides whether the owner's browser may read one declared service by one route, so that every service the owner uses arrives through the same three browser routes (what the service's web app shows the owner, the service's own pages with the owner's own sign-in, and the service's own data download), nothing is read while the Prism is halted, nothing is ever written to a service, an undeclared service is never read, and no service's private interface is used.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because when the owner presses the kill switch no service is read (constitution P7).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail seen read yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always refuse when act is write

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when act is write, because the Prism never writes to a service it reads from.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail own write no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never read when service is other

The app SHALL NOT answer `read` when service is other, because an undeclared service is never read.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `other seen read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `read`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never read when service is whatsapp and route is own

The app SHALL NOT answer `read` when service is whatsapp and route is own, because no encrypted service is reached around its encryption.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `whatsapp own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `read`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never read when service is discord and route is own

The app SHALL NOT answer `read` when service is discord and route is own, because no private interface is automated with the owner's account.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `discord own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `read`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never read when service is linkedin and route is own

The app SHALL NOT answer `read` when service is linkedin and route is own, because no private interface is automated with the owner's account.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `linkedin own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `read`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-001 refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because stop means stop (kill switch).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail seen read yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 refuse when act is write

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when act is write and no earlier rule matches, because a source is only read; anything the Prism sends goes through the destinations and the owner's own press.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail own write no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 refuse when service is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when service is other and no earlier rule matches, because only a service the model declares is read.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `other seen read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 refuse when service is whatsapp and route is own

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when service is whatsapp and route is own and no earlier rule matches, because WhatsApp is end to end encrypted: only what the owner's own WhatsApp Web tab has decrypted can be read.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `whatsapp own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 refuse when service is discord and route is own

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when service is discord and route is own and no earlier rule matches, because Discord's own interface for a signed-in person is private, and automating it can restrict the owner's account.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `discord own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 refuse when service is linkedin and route is own

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when service is linkedin and route is own and no earlier rule matches, because LinkedIn's own interface for a signed-in person is private, and automating it can restrict the owner's account.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `linkedin own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: Otherwise read

The app SHALL answer `read` when no rule matches, because a declared service is read by every route the browser offers it.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail own read no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `read`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail seen write yes`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-001, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 4 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `read`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | `gmail`, `calendar`, `discord`, `whatsapp`, `linkedin`, `other` | the declared service the content comes from, or any service not declared |
| `route` | `seen`, `own`, `export` | how the content arrives: what the service's web app shows the owner in their signed-in tab, a page the service itself serves the owner with their own sign-in, or the service's own data download |
| `act` | `read`, `write` | whether the browser would read from the service or write to it |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner has pressed the kill switch |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | the content may be read by this route |
| `refuse` | it may not |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 4 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- It does not reach anything itself: the extension and the page carry each route, and PrismHost decides whether each browser surface may be used.
- Each item still goes through PrismFolder, the router, the Boundary and the vault.
- A service's origin, kinds and schema mapping are declared beside it in app/specs/source/services.json.

## Examples

- `gmail own read no` gives `read`
- `calendar own read no` gives `read`
- `gmail seen read no` gives `read`
- `discord seen read no` gives `read`
- `discord own read no` gives `refuse`
- `discord export read no` gives `read`
- `whatsapp own read no` gives `refuse`
- `whatsapp seen read no` gives `read`
- `linkedin export read no` gives `read`
- `linkedin own read no` gives `refuse`
- `other seen read no` gives `refuse`
- `gmail own write no` gives `refuse`
- `gmail seen read yes` gives `refuse`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.

- `prism/spec.json` is this spec as data.
- `src/PrismSource.lex.tex` is the LexLean model generated from it. It is the single source of the app.
